policy.core: Objectives 2.1 through 2.3, their vocabulary, and their factual cases trace to Chapter 2 of the supplied textbook.
policy.supplement: Applications 2.4, 2.5 and 2.6 are explicitly labeled supplements, not textbook learning objectives. 2.4 places artificial intelligence inside the chapter's own value and advantage analysis. 2.5 makes the chapter's end-of-chapter spreadsheet and database exercises runnable on the page. 2.6 restates the chapter's analysis steps as executable functions and extends the database work across several tables; it introduces no new claims about the subject matter.
policy.hypotheticals: Practice situations are signposted as hypothetical. They may supply qualitative conditions needed for reasoning, but may not invent a real company, purport to report a real-world statistic, or blur a scenario assumption into a factual claim.
policy.currentLaw: This module makes no claims about current law.

chapter2.citation: Valacich & Schneider, Information Systems Today, 10th ed., Chapter 2, Enabling Organizational Strategy through Information Systems

chapter2Exercises.citation: Valacich & Schneider, Information Systems Today, 10th ed., Chapter 2, Application and Analytics Exercises
chapter2Exercises.relationship: The spreadsheet and database exercises the chapter sets; Application 2.5 makes them runnable.

porter1985.citation: Porter, M. E. (1985). Competitive Advantage: Creating and Sustaining Superior Performance. Free Press.
porter1985.relationship: The competitive-forces and value-chain analysis Chapter 2 presents originates here.
